subject: Re: Legal sync — delegated ops & evidence path for private deployment
messages:
From: Sofia Ruiz <sofia.ruiz@medtech.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-legal@medtech.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment — evidence & operator access questions

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our security and procurement teams reviewed the draft MSA + Order Form and flagged two items we need clarity on before we proceed:

1) Evidence access model: we need a clear pathway showing how Redwood will provide proof of correct key custody and the ability to inspect runbooks in a private (VPC) deployment. Our compliance team asked if there is an "escrow-like" option (snapshot + third-party verification) and whether Redwood can commit to a quarterly attestation.

2) Operator boundary: the current addendum language appears to give operator access for support under broad terms. We need tighter scope (list of allowed actions, jump host restrictions, and temporary access windows with audit logs).

Can you share a proposed timeline for responses and whether your legal/ops teams are comfortable with a limited escrow-style mechanism?

Attachments: MedTech_DueDiligence_List_20270520.pdf (attachment)

Best,
Sofia Ruiz
Head of IT Security — MedTech Systems
sofia.ruiz@medtech.com

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ruiz <sofia.ruiz@medtech.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment — evidence & operator access questions

Sofia — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, then looping in Legal/Prod Ops for details:

- Escrow-like snapshot: we can provide periodic immutable snapshots of the deployment metadata (operator audit logs, KV-cache hashes, and snapshot manifests). Full handoff of binaries or data is not something we do routinely, but we have an established third-party attestation workflow that many regulated customers use.

- Quarterly attestation: yes, we can commit to a signed quarterly attestation covering access events and configuration integrity for the reserved environment.

- Operator boundary: agree on tighter language — short-term jump-host access with timeboxed SSH sessions, MFA enforced via customer-managed IdP, and all sessions recorded and stored for 180 days by default.

I'll attach our proposed redlines and a matrix mapping the evidence we can provide. Laura — can you review the redlines and advise on the MSA addendum language and whether a limited escrow clause is acceptable? Aditya — can you confirm the technical feasibility of immutable snapshot manifests and the typical delivery cadence?

Thanks,
Logan
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_Redlines_20270521.pdf; evidence_matrix_medtech.xlsx

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Private deployment — evidence & operator access questions

Logan / Aditya — forwarding Sofia's note and Logan's initial reply. My take (high level):

- Escrow-like mechanism: legal is wary of language that implies transfer of IP or source; we can offer a controlled-snapshot + third-party attestation (SOC-type independent verifier) that verifies the snapshot manifests and operator activity. Draft clause should be explicit that snapshots are metadata and attestations only — not source code or model weights.

- Attestation cadence: quarterly signed attestations are fine. Recommend adding a limited-scope SLA for delivery (e.g., attestation delivered within 20 business days of quarter close) and a mutual NDA for the attestation artifacts.

- Operator boundary: we need precise definitions in the addendum: "Support Operator" role (enumerate permitted actions), access methods (SSH via customer jump-host with just-in-time role elevation), and strict logging & session retention. No standing operator keys; all access granted via time-limited tokens.

I made redline suggestions in the attached PDF (see notes on Section 3.2 and Section 7.1). Also flagged liability caps for any evidence-related disclosure — we should not open unlimited liability if a snapshot manifest has issues.

Next steps: Logan, send MedTech a short summary of what we will commit to (attestation cadence, snapshot types, operator constraints) and propose a two-week schedule for legal to redline and for ops to entregar the first sample manifest.

- Laura
VP Legal, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment — evidence & operator access questions

Couple of technical notes from Prod Ops:

- Snapshot contents: we can generate a signed manifest that includes: deployed model checksum (quantized artifact hash), active configuration (container image IDs, runtime flags), operator audit log (actions with timestamps and user IDs), and KV-cache HMACs for prefix acceptance checks. No model weights or customer data are included in the manifest.

- Delivery cadence: we can provide a monthly manifest and a quarterly immutable archive (for attestation) — that should satisfy both the operational and compliance asks.

- Verification: we typically onboard a neutral third-party auditor to perform the verification of manifests. We have a partner (SecureAssure) that already understands our format and can sign an attestation. If MedTech prefers a different auditor, we can coordinate.

- Timing: generating an initial sample manifest for review will take ~6 business days.

Happy to jump on a call with MedTech's security team next week.

— Aditya
Senior Product Ops Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ruiz <sofia.ruiz@medtech.com>
Cc: ops-legal@medtech.com, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 11:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment — evidence & operator access questions

Sofia — thanks for the patience. Summary / commitments from Redwood:

1) Evidence & attestation
- We will deliver monthly signed manifests (metadata-only) and maintain a quarterly immutable archive that an independent auditor can verify. Manifests include model artifact checksums, runtime config, operator audit logs (IDs + timestamps), and KV-cache HMACs. No model weights or customer data will be included.
- We propose SecureAssure as the neutral verifier; if MedTech prefers another firm, we can coordinate.
- Quarterly attestation will be signed and delivered within 20 business days of quarter close.

2) Operator access constraints
- Support Operator role limited to enumerated actions (incident diagnosis, configuration patching with change request, and service restarts).
- Access only via customer-managed jump host with MFA and just-in-time tokens; no standing operator keys.
- All sessions are recorded and retained for 180 days; export of recordings requires a legal request and is governed by the attestation NDA.

3) Draft redlines and timeline
- Attached: Redwood_MSA_Redlines_20270521.pdf (aggregated redlines) and evidence_matrix_medtech.xlsx (mapping).
- Proposed schedule: MedTech to review these redlines and confirm auditor preference by 05/28; Redwood to produce a sample manifest by 06/01 for joint review. Legal redlines resolved by 06/11 so procurement can sign the Order Form by 06/18.

If this matches MedTech's needs, please confirm and we'll open a short working channel (weekly 30-minute touchpoints) to iterate the addendum.

Best,
Logan
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
